title: Osso Buco
subtitle: Braised veal shin with gremolata
excerpt: Thick cross-cut veal shin braised until the meat is falling off the bone in a sauce of white wine, tomato, and vegetable. Finished with gremolata of lemon zest, garlic, and parsley.

recipe.sourceNotes: Osso buco ('hollow bone' in Italian) is a Milanese speciality of braised veal shanks cut across the bone. The central marrow bone, which gives the dish its name, is the prized element: the richly flavoured marrow is scooped out with a small spoon and spread onto bread or stirred into the sauce. The dish is traditionally served with risotto alla Milanese (saffron risotto) and finished with gremolata, a sharp garnish of raw lemon zest, garlic, and parsley that cuts through the richness of the braise.

content.text: The veal pieces should be tied around the circumference with kitchen string to stop them from falling apart during the long braise: the meat pulls away from the bone as it cooks. Brown the seasoned flour-dusted shanks in hot oil until deeply caramelised before adding the liquid. The gremolata should be made fresh and added only at the table, not cooked in the sauce.

items.preparation: 4 cross-cut bone-in pieces about 4 cm thick; ask butcher for veal shin (osso buco cut) if available

content.text: Season the veal pieces and dust with flour. Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the veal on both sides until deeply caramelised, about 4 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
Reduce to medium. Soften the onion, celery, and carrot for 10 minutes. Add the garlic. Cook for 1 minute. Pour in the wine and bubble for 3 minutes.

Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, thyme, and bay leaves. Return the veal, standing the pieces upright so the marrow does not fall out. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over the lowest heat for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours until the meat is very tender.
Make the gremolata by mixing the lemon zest, minced garlic, and parsley. Serve the osso buco over risotto Milanese. Scatter the gremolata over each serving.
